quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson on the impact of the new CBA
quotes.excerpt: It's the CBA. That's the only thing I've been trying to like point out to you guys.
quotes.quote: It's the CBA. That's the only thing I've been trying to like point out to you guys the whole time. With the new CBA, if I don't have to, I'm not going to do it. Because at the end of the day, that literally strongholds what you can do in the future. And if he is the only guys that are going to get paid from here on out with the way the CBA is negotiated right now, the only guys that are going to get big paydays are the Tatums, the Shays, the Ants, the superstars. The got your franchise guys are going to be making that.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson on the trade rumors involving Kevin Durant
quotes.excerpt: I just don't want to see him go nowhere else. It's been too many teams as it is.
quotes.quote: I just don't want to see him go nowhere else. It's been too many teams as it is, especially with the talent like that. Figure it out, see what you can do, right off to the sunset, my boy.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson questions the influence of NBA analytics on player evaluation
quotes.excerpt: I didn't know analytics guys had that much power. This is crazy. When did this league become straight analytics?
quotes.quote: I didn't know analytics guys had that much power. This is crazy. When did this league become straight analytics? I knew we had it in ours, but I didn't know it determined so much. When did the eye test and understanding the game of basketball, what someone can bring to your team, a mentality, putting the ball in the basket, how they can change how other people compete, how other people play the game of basketball, when did that part -- what analytics control that too? Can they tell you that?

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson questions the analytical view of the Boston Celtics as the second seed
quotes.excerpt: I wanted the analytics guys to tell me why they saw Boston as number two in the East.
quotes.quote: I wanted the analytics guys to tell me why they saw Boston as number two in the East. Analytically, I know they didn't say that. So how can you determine how Jaylen Brown is as a player and how he affects his teammates, how he brings the best out of his teammates? Like I said, I don't know what happened in the locker room, but there's one thing that you can't say he did not do. He led the team to number two in the East.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson defends Jaylen Brown's impact on the Boston Celtics
quotes.excerpt: Kobe Bryant is not the easiest person to play with, but he's elevated a lot of guys.
quotes.quote: If you're going to determine somebody on how they are, like, Kobe Bryant is not the easiest person to play with, but he's elevated a lot of guys where they get him five championships. Michael Jordan is not the easiest player to play with. Analytically, would Michael Jordan look good? We don't fucking know. But Jaylen Brown won a lot of fucking games. It's not like Jaylen Brown has been a loser, right? He was number two in the East. I thought analytics are going towards winning. How does this guy's analytics not look good if he's winning?

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson argues for valuing player contributions over analytics
quotes.excerpt: I would rather people say it's the money than it is his analytics.
quotes.quote: I would rather people say it's the money than it is his analytics. Because at the end of the day, you need a guy like Jaylen Brown who plays on both ends of the floor, who competes, can put the ball in the basket. I mean, the guy was in the MVP race, guys. What the fuck are we talking about? That that shit makes no sense to me.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson questions why the Charlotte Hornets would change their team culture
quotes.excerpt: Why when you give them that and you saw what that team can do, do you throw that away?
quotes.quote: Why when you give them that and you saw what that team can do, do you throw that away? That's my true question. You never had this before. You didn't have a structure, you didn't have anything that was, oh, this is the Hornets way here. Why when you give them that and you saw what that team can do, do you throw that away? That's my true question.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson argues for the importance of team culture and leadership
quotes.excerpt: I think the Hornets are going to realize LaMelo Ball is more pivotal for the vibe of the team.
quotes.quote: I think the Hornets are going to realize LaMelo Ball is more pivotal for the vibe of the team, for the confidence he brought to his teammates. It's something you can't really replace. At the end of the day, what's a good team you had? And then what's a good team that you had and you lost a player and you're like, oh yeah, now that we lost him, we going to struggle.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson

quotes.quote: I don't truly understand the comment that he's too smart for his own good. Do you want him to be stupid? Do you want him not to be smart? I don't think there's nobody saying they don't want to be smart.

quotes.quote: They want you to just fall in line. Don't cause no controversy. Don't say nothing crazy. I'm not saying they don't want you to be smart, but they want you to just fall in line. Don't cause no controversy. Don't say nothing crazy.
